newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM NOT AGAINST TURKEY'S EU MEMBERSHIP BID.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM NOT AGAINST TURKEY'S EU MEMBERSHIP BID.

text.p: Turkey cannot be excluded from membership of the European Union on geographical, religious or language grounds, the Belgian foreign ministry said on Wednsday.

"Belgium has always subscribed to the idea that Turkey is destined to belong to Europe, provided it meets a number of political and economical criteria," foreign ministry spokesman Andre Querton told reporters at a briefing.
He said Turkey would have to make progress in human rights, the Kurdish issue and its relations with Cyprus, but added there could be no objections in principle to Turkey.
"There is no reason to exclude any country (from the EU) on the basis of language, religion or geography," Querton said.
Turkey's longstanding efforts to join the EU will be on the agenda of an informal meeting of EU foreign affairs ministers in the Dutch town of Apeldoorn this weekend.

The issue is thornier than ever after German chancellor Helmut Kohl and other centrist EU leaders said at a meeting of Christian-Democratic politicians last week that Turkey should not be allowed into the EU.
At the meeting, Wilfried Martens, leader of the European People's Party and former Belgian prime minister, made it plain that Turkey was not seen as a part of Europe.
"We are creating a European Union, that is a European project," Martens said.

Asked about comments by Martens who reportedly said that Turkey cannot join because it belongs to a different civilisation, Querton said that he was not aware of any such criteria in the EU's founding treaties.

A small part of Turkey's vast landmass is on the European subcontinent. While the 15 nation EU-block is a Babylon of languages, all member states -- while officialy secular states -- have a Christian history.
If Turkey's bid to join the EU were successful, it would be the first member country with a predominantly moslem population.
"It is striking that with regard to bids by other countries, the debate always focuses on practical matters, while for Turkey it is a matter of principle," Querton said.
The French government on Monday also distanced itself from the European Christian Democratic leaders' "no" to Turkey.

It used no geopolitical or philosophical arguments, but said that for the sake of the stability of Europe, the Turks should be allowed to retain a European prospect, even if membership would not be realistic in the short term.
The French also warned NATO-member Turkey against blocking further NATO enlargement in order to force its way into Europe.
